concepts.def: One God in three persons: Father, Son and Holy Spirit
All-powerful — God can do anything logically possible
God made the universe ex nihilo (out of nothing)
Six days of ordered creation; God saw it was good
John 1 — through the Word all things were made

walkthroughs.body_html:
Christians believe in one God in three persons.

The Father creates and sustains. The Son (Jesus) saves. The Holy Spirit guides and inspires believers today.

This is not three gods — it's one God revealed in three ways. The Nicene Creed sums it up.

God is omnipotent (all-powerful), omniscient (all-knowing), and omnibenevolent (all-loving).

God is also just — fair, rewarding good and judging evil.

These qualities raise questions: if God is all-loving and all-powerful, why does evil exist? (We'll come back to that.)

Genesis 1: 'In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.' Six days, ordered, and God called it 'good'.

Genesis 2 focuses on humans — Adam formed from dust, given the Garden of Eden.

John 1 adds: 'In the beginning was the Word... through him all things were made' — linking creation to Jesus.
